verdict.rationale: Gmail filters are documented as rules evaluated against incoming messages using criteria like sender, subject, or size. When a message matches, the filter automatically triggers actions such as adding or removing labels or forwarding. API push notifications on mailbox changes also let developers attach custom automated actions in their own backend. Missing for 10: the documented action set is narrow (labels and forwarding); custom actions require building your own server; there is no evidence of AI or natural-language rule authoring; there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.
